reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses AlNbTiZr medium-entropy alloy coatings on Zr-alloy, showing Al content influences corrosion resistance in high-temperature water, but it does not address Al ion implantation into pure Cr, post-implantation annealing, Al segregation to a Cr/Zr interface, or the formation of a diffusion barrier against Cr-Zr interdiffusion. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Aluminum ion implantation into a Cr coating can be achieved with the specified parameters.
Post-implantation annealing will cause Al to segregate to the Cr/Zr interface.
The segregated Al will form a stable Al-rich phase or mixed Cr-Al oxide at the interface.
This Al-rich interfacial phase will act as an effective diffusion barrier against Cr-Zr interdiffusion at ~1200°C.
The Al-implanted and annealed Cr coating will retain corrosion resistance in subcritical water at ~320°C.
